name: Select-service hotel
summary: Branded 4–5 story select/limited-service hotel (Hampton / Courtyard class) of ~80–160 keys with breakfast area, small meeting room, fitness and pool; cost is driven by guestroom count, framing system (wood vs. concrete/steel) and market. Data quality is good: four editions of the HVS U.S. Hotel Development Cost Survey (2022–2025 data) give national per-key medians by component, cross-checked with RLB Q2 2026 3-star $/SF and an HVS feasibility budget. HVS building costs include permits, engineering and hard contingency, so they are scaled to our hard-cost definition.

typicalSize.method: HVS Murrieta feasibility recommends 120 rooms (e27); HCEG midscale prototype 135 rooms, economy 90 (e28). Typical branded select-service runs ~80–160 keys; mid 115.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross building SF per key = net guestroom (HCEG midscale 370 SF, upscale 389 SF, e29) + bath (~45–55 SF) ≈ 420–440 SF, divided by a ~0.65–0.75 guestroom share of GSF (double-loaded corridors, compact public/BOH) ≈ 560–680 SF; mid 620.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: A 4–5 story, ~115-key, ~71,000 GSF building has a ~15,000–18,000 SF footprint; with ~1.0 surface space/key (~350 SF each incl. aisles) plus pool/landscape/setbacks the site is ~2–3 acres → ~40–60 keys/acre; 70 for tighter suburban sites, 35 for 3-story.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: HCEG prototypes park 1.11 spaces/room (economy 100/90, midscale 150/135) (e30); urban/transit sites often 0.6–0.8; local code governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS building & site improvements per key, national (median / average): 2025 data select-service $126,900 / $156,219 (e1), limited-service $141,143 / $136,162 (e2); 2024 data select $159,636 / $167,381 (e3), limited $111,846 / $111,549 (e4); earlier editions ~$161k medians (e5, e6). The median of the 2024–2025 select + limited figures is ~$139k. HVS includes building permits, engineering and hard-cost contingency, so x0.91 converts to contractor price (≈ remove ~5% contingency and ~4% permits/engineering) → ~$126k; nudged up to $140k because HVS budgets skew to secondary/suburban markets and RLB metro 3-star costs are far higher (e8: median ~$406/SF x 620 SF ≈ $250k). Low $100k ≈ 0.91 x 2024 limited-service median (~$102k) / Murrieta comparable minimum $88k (2022, e7). High $230k ≈ RLB 3-star lower-metro level (~$370/SF x 620 SF) and 0.91 x 2023 select-service average ($187k → $170k) plus urban premium. Dollar year 2025 (HVS 2026 edition); 2024-data figures are within one year.

perSF.method: Mid = $140k/key ÷ 620 SF/key ≈ $226/SF. Cross-checks: RSMeans 4–7 story hotel model $181–$197/SF in 2019 dollars incl. 25% contractor fees and 6% A/E, building only (e11); RLB 2026 3-star hotels in large metros $230–$685/SF, Phoenix $230–$350, Dallas $310–$455, 18-city median midpoint $406 (e8, e10, e9). Wood-frame suburban select-service sits near the low end of RLB ranges. Low = $100k/620; high ≈ RLB median-of-lows to midpoint ($343–$406).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P and typical on-site work (surface parking, outdoor pool, landscaping, on-site utilities); excludes land, soft costs, FF&E/OS&E, pre-opening, permits, contingency, off-sites, impact/tap fees and financing.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ low/mid ($100k/$140k ≈ 0.71, rounded to 0.75 — HVS midscale extended-stay/limited-service medians ~$110k); premium ≈ upscale select / dual-brand (~1.3); luxury tier = high/mid ($230k/$140k ≈ 1.65), i.e., urban upscale select-service.

systemSplit.method: No public elemental breakdown was found. Derived for a 4–5 story wood-frame (podium-less) select-service hotel with ~10% sitework: framing/rough carpentry (06) and finishes (09) largest; per-room bathrooms and PTAC/VTAC drive plumbing (22) and HVAC (23); elevators (14) two cabs; laundry/breakfast equipment fixed portion (11); vanities/casework (12); general conditions (01) ~8% with OH&P distributed into trades. Verify against a contractor GMP schedule of values.

lineItems.name: Pre-opening, OS&E and working capital

cost.method: HVS pre-opening & working capital per key: 2025 data select $3,561 median / $5,477 avg (e20), limited $2,900 / $3,690 (e21); 2024 data select $5,894 / $6,454 (e22); Murrieta budget $4,000 (2022, e23). Mid ≈ midpoint of the medians/averages.

lineItems.notes: Owner cost, not construction: operating reserves, pre-opening staffing/training, OS&E (linen, operating supplies), technical services fees (HVS categories). Treat as a soft/owner line.

lineItems.name: Brand monument sign

cost.method: HCEG 2021 midscale/extended-stay monument sign $11,948–$17,563 each (e31), x1.18 for the GC markups the guide excludes → ~$14.1k–$20.7k.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of baseline; brand standard sign packages vary.

lineItems.name: Highway / pylon sign

cost.method: HCEG 2021 highway sign $23,895–$32,617 (e32) x1.18 GC markup.

lineItems.notes: Interstate-oriented sites only; local sign code governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS FF&E per key: 2025 data select $18,321 median / $22,860 avg (e12), limited $16,079 / $18,020 (e13); 2024 data select $22,929 / $23,120 (e14); Murrieta $17,000 (2022, comparables $13.6k–$20.0k, e15). Mid ≈ median of the HVS medians/averages. Includes laundry and breakfast kitchen equipment and technology; OS&E is in pre-opening.

pctOfHard.method: HVS soft cost ÷ building & site improvements (medians): select 2025 data 21,002/126,900 = 16.5% (e16); limited 19,896/141,143 = 14.1% (e17); select 2024 data 24,833/159,636 = 15.6% (e18); Murrieta 30,000/120,000 = 25% (e19). HVS soft costs include construction financing (excluded here, ~4–6% of hard) while HVS building costs include permits/engineering (soft here, ~3–4%) — roughly offsetting, so mid 16%. Excludes developer fee (HVS median $9,500/key select-service).

softCosts.notes: Type-specific soft items inside this %: brand franchise application/initial fee and brand design-review/technical-services fees (HVS lists the franchise application fee under soft costs; amount is brand- and key-count-specific — take it from the brand FDD), interior design, hospitality consultants/feasibility study. Developer fee and financing are handled outside this %.

design.method: Prototype brand plans are well-defined, so design contingency is modest; 10% at concept stage before brand plan selection.

hard.method: Typical new-construction owner hard-cost contingency for repetitive prototype hotels; HVS budgets carry a hard-cost contingency inside building costs (removed from our hard cost by the x0.91 factor).

soft.method: Typical soft-cost contingency norm; HVS lists a soft-cost contingency within soft costs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS all-in total less land: select-service 2025 data $200,730 − $18,000 = ~$183k median, $239,006 − $21,871 = ~$217k average (e24); limited-service ~$175k median (e25); 2024 data select ~$207k median (e26). These include FF&E, pre-opening, financing and developer fee. Min/max widen for small-market limited-service and urban/high-cost metros.

openQuestions: A public GMP / schedule of values for a 2024–2026 select-service hotel would replace the derived CSI split.
Brand FDD (Item 5/7) initial franchise fee and PIP/technical-services fees per brand were not collected — search budget ran out.
Gross SF per key is derived from HCEG guestroom sizes; a brand prototype program (GSF and key count) would firm up $/SF.
